newsitem.title: FRANCE: Elf to sell Renault shares in asset sale drive.
newsitem.headline: Elf to sell Renault shares in asset sale drive.

text.p: Oil group Elf Aquitaine SA on Thursday said it planned to sell its remaining 1.2 percent stake in carmaker Renault SA as part of its drive to sell financial assets.
Elf obtained the shares during the first stage of Renault's partial privatisation in November 1994 when a number of core shareholders bought shares at 179.50 francs.
Elf had held a 1.5 percent stake in Renault, but it has been gradually reduced this year.
Elf's existing stake of 2,868,126 shares was worth 514.83 million francs when it was bought and 505.94 million francs on Thursday as Renault shares traded in late morning at 176.40 francs.
The other core shareholders of Renault have 10 days to exercise their right of first refusal. If they do not want to buy the shares, Elf can sell in the market.

The other Renault core shareholders are Lagardere Groupe, BNP, Rhone-Poulenc, CDC, Union Bank of Switzerland, CCF, AGF, Lazard, Credit National, Bayerische Landesbank, B C Vaudoise, CCBP, ING and Commerzbank.
Elf had a stake in Renault as part of the "core" or "stable" group of shareholders the conservative government of Edouard Balladur set up as part of its privatisation programme.
Renault sold its stake in Elf on May 21 this year. The car maker made a 400 million franc capital gain on selling 2.5 million shares, or 0.9 percent, to Elf unit Financiere Valorgest.

Elf chairman Philippe Jaffre has made the sale of non-strategic and financial assets one of his key priorities since he assumed the helm of the group in 1993. The group has raised 11 billion francs in asset sales since its privatisation in 1994.

The biggest operations were the sale of stakes in Enterprise Oil in Britain and Petrofina in Belgium and more recently the sale of a stake in Compagnie de Suez and the planned market float of the ISIS oil services company.
What remains are stakes in engineering companies Technip, 3.1 percent, and Coflexip, in which it has a 1.1 percent direct stake while chemicals unit Elf Atochem has 3.1 percent.
The group also has a small stake in Spain's Banco Central Hispanoamericano SA following a deal concerning the Cepsa refinery.
It holds a stake in bank BNP, also as part of a core group at the time of the bank's privatisation, and BNP chairman Michel Pebereau sits on the Elf board.
Jaffre said in May that the capital gains on the group's 3.5 billion franc of assets in its financial portfolio could potentially be as much as 400 million francs.
"The current stakes are now stable but by 2005 I don't think we'll have them," he said in May.

Apart from the financial stakes, Jaffre has said he is willing to let the group's stake in health and beauty products group Sanofi fall from its current 53 percent to below 50 percent if the unit were to strike an alliance deal.

Elf obtained the stakes when it was state-owned and run by Loik Le Floch Prigent. At the time Elf was not only following corporate policies but was also an instrument of economic policy for the French state.
During that time Elf also concluded a deal with the Treuhandstad privatisation agency concerning the Leuna refinery which is expected to come on stream later this year.
Jaffre cut Elf's investment in Leuna and had difficult talks with the Russian partners in the deal who were unable to pay-up their part of the investments.

On Wednesday, the European Union Commission said it had started a probe into some 1.4 billion marks in subsidies received by Elf to build the refinery after a disagreement with Truehand successor BvS over the real costs of the project.
